'''Bryce Jiron Cotton''' (born August 11, 1992) is an American-Australian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). As a member of the [[Perth Wildcats]] between 2017 and 2025, he won three [[List of NBL champions|NBL championships]] and five [[NBL Most Valuable Player Award]]s. In 2026, he won his sixth NBL MVP as a member of the 36ers. He is also a two-time [[NBL Grand Final Most Valuable Player Award|NBL Grand Final MVP]], nine-time [[All-NBL Team|All-NBL First Team]] recipient, and has collected nine [[List of National Basketball League (Australia) annual scoring leaders|NBL scoring titles]].

Cotton played [[college basketball]] for four seasons with the [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence Friars]], where he was a two-time first-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] honoree in 2013 and 2014. After going undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]], Cotton had a number of short stints in the [[NBA]] over his first two professional seasons, playing for the [[Utah Jazz]], [[Phoenix Suns]] and [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. He also played in the [[NBA Development League]], China, Turkey and Italy between 2014 and 2018.

Cotton arrived in Australia to play for the Wildcats midway through the [[2016–17 NBL season]], going on to lead Perth to the NBL championship in the [[2017 NBL Finals]] behind a grand final MVP performance. After winning his first league MVP in [[2017–18 NBL season|2018]], he won his second and third NBL championships in [[2018–19 NBL season|2019]] and [[2019–20 NBL season|2020]] while also garnering his second NBL MVP and second grand final MVP in 2020. He won his third, fourth and fifth NBL MVPs in [[2020–21 NBL season|2021]], [[2023–24 NBL season|2024]] and [[2024–25 NBL season|2025]] respectively. In 2025, he set a club record with his seventh Wildcats Club MVP.

After nine seasons with the Wildcats, Cotton joined the Adelaide 36ers in 2025 and in the [[2025–26 NBL season|2025–26 season]], he collected his sixth NBL MVP, coming within one of [[Andrew Gaze]]'s all-time best seven league MVPs.

In 2025, Cotton became an Australian citizen. The following year, he debuted for the [[Australia men's national basketball team]].

==Early life==
Cotton was born and raised in [[Tucson, Arizona]].<ref name=my-story>{{cite web|url=https://www.brycecotton.com.au/pages/my-story|title=My Story|work=brycecotton.com.au|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211219121903/https://www.brycecotton.com.au/pages/my-story|archive-date=December 19, 2021}}</ref><ref name=weapon>{{cite web|last=O'Donoghue|first=Craig|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/perth-wildcats/nbl-playoffs-perth-wildcats-star-bryce-cottons-secret-weapon-ng-b88755543z|title=NBL playoffs: Perth Wildcats star Bryce Cotton's secret weapon|work=[[The West Australian]]|date=March 3, 2018|access-date=June 7, 2018}}</ref> His parents separated when he was a toddler and his father worked as a police officer on the other side of the country. He reconnected with his father in New York while in college.<ref name="weapon" /> His uncle, former [[National Football League|NFL]] player [[David Adams (gridiron football)|David Adams]], often provided the family with financial assistance during tough times. Cotton's grandmother, Mary, helped raise him and his brother Justin while their mother worked in real estate.<ref name="weapon" />

Cotton loved sports as a child, playing basketball, [[American football|football]] and [[baseball]].<ref name="my-story" /> He was advised during fifth grade to no longer play football due to the high risk of head injuries which could lead to seizures.<ref name="my-story" /> He was diagnosed with a rare form of [[epilepsy]]<ref>{{cite news |title=The deadly health battle that inspires Bryce Cotton |url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/perth-wildcats/how-bryce-cotton-survived-a-potentially-deadly-childhood-health-battle-to-dominate-the-nbl-ng-b881687628z |access-date=7 November 2024 |work=The West Australian |date=7 October 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Cotton details his extraordinary battle with epilepsy |url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/perth-wildcats/perth-wildcats-star-bryce-cotton-details-his-extraordinary-battle-with-epilepsy-ng-b881706398z |access-date=7 November 2024 |work=The West Australian |date=29 October 2020 |language=en}}</ref> and his mother was told that he "wasn't going to make it past sixth grade, and that she should start planning for the funeral".<ref name=Wildie>{{cite web|last=Wildie|first=Tom|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-12-21/bryce-cotton-childhood-epilepsy-nba-nbl-basketball/103235534|title=Childhood illness threatened Bryce Cotton's life, but set him on a path to basketball glory|work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]]|date=December 21, 2023|access-date=December 21, 2023}}</ref> The last seizure Cotton experienced was on his final day of sixth grade. He remained on medication for several years, but eventually no longer required treatment.<ref name="Wildie" />

Focusing on basketball, one of Cotton's biggest deficiencies was his lack of height. He worked with his uncle for an edge to combat taller opponents<ref name="weapon" /> and modelled his game on NBA star [[Allen Iverson]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=O'Donoghue |first1=Craig |title=Bryce Cotton's love for Allen Iverson was one of the key reasons the NBL asked him to come to HoopsFest |url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/basketball/bryce-cottons-love-for-allen-iverson-was-one-of-the-key-reasons-the-nbl-asked-him-to-come-to-hoopsfest-c-21273139 |access-date=11 January 2026 |work=The West Australian |date=11 January 2026 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20260111070807/https://thewest.com.au/sport/basketball/bryce-cottons-love-for-allen-iverson-was-one-of-the-key-reasons-the-nbl-asked-him-to-come-to-hoopsfest-c-21273139 |archive-date=11 January 2026 |language=en |url-status=dead}}</ref> He spent much of his youth on outdoor basketball courts playing pick-up games.<ref>{{cite web|last=O'Donoghue|first=Craig|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/nbl/perth-wildcats-star-bryce-cotton-says-basketball-saved-his-life-as-he-celebrates-world-basketball-day-c-12968307|title=Perth Wildcats star Bryce Cotton says basketball saved his life as he celebrates World Basketball Day|work=[[The West Australian]]|date=December 21, 2023|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20231221004618/https://thewest.com.au/sport/nbl/perth-wildcats-star-bryce-cotton-says-basketball-saved-his-life-as-he-celebrates-world-basketball-day-c-12968307|archive-date=December 21, 2023}}</ref>

==High school career==
After spending his junior year in [[Las Vegas]],<ref name="my-story" /> Cotton completed secondary school at [[Palo Verde High School (Arizona)|Palo Verde High School]] in Tucson. Cotton helped lead Palo Verde to a 24–7 record and a berth in the state 4A semifinals in the 2009–10 season. He averaged 23.6 points, 7.5 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 3.7 steals per game as a senior,<ref name=maxpreps>{{cite web|last=Morgan|first=Craig|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/P_liNraiEd-YiQAcxJSkrA/chandlers-hundley-to-decide-between-ucla-and-washington.htm|title=Chandler's Hundley to decide between UCLA and Washington|work=MaxPreps.com|date=September 2, 2010|access-date=February 16, 2014}}</ref> and scored 30 or more points nine times, including a career-high 40 points in an 85–82 win over [[Buckeye Union High School|Buckeye]] on February 16, 2010. He also set a school record for the highest triple-double with 37 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists against [[Rio Rico High School|Rio Rico]] on December 11, 2009. He earned First Team All-City and First Team All-State honors in 2010.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.friars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/cotton_bryce00.html|title=11 Bryce Cotton|work=Friars.com|access-date=June 7, 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143841/http://www.friars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/cotton_bryce00.html|archive-date=June 12, 2018}}</ref> He also had perfect grades and a high [[Grading in education|GPA]].<ref name="my-story" />

Cotton was not highly recruited out of high school.<ref name=nytimes2>{{cite web|last=Giles|first=Matt|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/13/sports/ncaabasketball/providences-inexhaustible-point-guard-almost-never-leaves-the-court.html|title=Providence's Inexhaustible Point Guard Almost Never Leaves the Court|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 12, 2014|access-date=June 7, 2018}}</ref> He was turned down by [[Montana State Bobcats men's basketball|Montana State]] and [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball|Northern Arizona]], and was later also turned away by [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] school [[Chico State Wildcats|Chico State]].<ref name="my-story" /> He also reportedly tried to obtain a scholarship from [[Houston Baptist Huskies men's basketball|Houston Baptist]].<ref name=card>{{cite web|last=Rutherford|first=Mike|url=https://www.cardchronicle.com/2013/1/2/3828688/the-bryce-cotton-saga-a-history|title=The Bryce Cotton Saga: A History|work=CardChronicle.com|date=January 2, 2013|access-date=June 7, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==

===Freshman season===
Cotton's family could not afford to pay for college tuition and his scholarship dream looked over until [[Providence College]] made an offer just three days before freshman orientation.<ref name="weapon" /> After reportedly signing with [[Miami Dade College]] on August 18, 2010,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tucson.com/sports/palo-verde-grad-cotton-accepts-full-ride-at-miami-dade/article_3c37e35b-a4ef-5c1c-917f-71b37b0cec13.html|title=Palo Verde grad Cotton accepts full ride at Miami Dade|work=Tucson.com|date=August 18, 2010|access-date=June 7, 2018}}</ref> Cotton instead committed to the [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence Friars]] on August 30.<ref name="maxpreps" /><ref name="card" /> He scored 15 points in the Friars' season opener against [[Dartmouth Big Green men's basketball|Dartmouth]] on November 13, 2010.<ref name="bio" /> He was a bench player in his freshman season and was unable to break through in a rotation that featured [[MarShon Brooks]], [[Vincent Council]], [[Gerard Coleman]] and [[Duke Mondy]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fischer |first1=Jake |title=Bryce Cotton: Second Round Steal |url=https://www.slamonline.com/news/nba/bryce-cotton-providence-nba-draft/ |access-date=15 January 2025 |work=SLAM |date=30 May 2014 |language=en}}</ref> In 31 games in 2010–11, Cotton averaged 4.0 points and 1.5 rebounds in 15.3 minutes per game.<ref name=stats>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/bryce-cotton-1.html|title=Bryce Cotton College Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=June 7, 2018}}</ref>

===Sophomore season===
As a sophomore in 2011–12, Cotton became a starter and was the team's second leading scorer, averaging 14.3 points per game while shooting 37.9 percent from 3-point range.<ref name="stats" /><ref name=breport>{{cite web|last=Kelley|first=Jimmy|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1140844-providence-basketball-roster-overhaul-continues-as-friars-lose-bryce-cotton|title=Providence Basketball: Roster Overhaul Continues as Friars Lose Bryce Cotton|work=BleacherReport.com|date=April 12, 2012|access-date=June 7, 2018}}</ref> On December 10, 2011, Cotton scored 20 of his career-high 34 points in the first half of the Friars' 72–61 win over [[Bryant Bulldogs men's basketball|Bryant]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/12/11/sports/ncaabasketball/no-7-duke-manages-to-hold-off-washington-at-garden.html|title=It's Perilous at the Top as No. 1 Kentucky and No. 2 Ohio State Lose|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=December 10, 2011|access-date=June 7, 2018}}</ref> He went 11-of-16 from the field with a perfect 10-of-10 from the [[free throw]] line against Bryant.<ref name="bio" /> He later scored 27 points on 5-of-6 shooting from the field, with a perfect 5-of-5 from 3-point range and 10-of-12 from the free throw line against [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] on January 10, 2012.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="card" />

===Junior season===
Despite reports of Cotton leaving Providence following his sophomore season,<ref name="breport" /><ref>{{cite web|last=Payne|first=Terrence|url=http://bigeast360.com/reports-providence-sophomore-bryce-cotton-to-transfer/|title=Reports: Providence sophomore Bryce Cotton to transfer|work=bigeast360.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102105412/http://bigeast360.com/reports-providence-sophomore-bryce-cotton-to-transfer/|archive-date=November 2, 2012}}</ref> he continued on with the Friars in 2012–13.<ref name="my-story" />

Following a breakout sophomore year, Cotton came into his junior season still in the shadows of senior point guard Vincent Council. Cotton was forced to step into the forefront for Providence to make up for injuries in the backcourt to Council and highly touted freshman guard [[Kris Dunn]].<ref name=ustoday>{{cite web|last=Joseph|first=Kevin|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/bigeast/2013/01/24/bryce-cotton-providence-basketball-interview/1863397/|title=Getting to know: Providence Friars guard Bryce Cotton|work=USAToday.com|date=January 24, 2013|access-date=June 7, 2018}}</ref> Cotton also had to take on a leadership role with a young team.<ref name="ustoday" /> He registered his first career double-double with 24 points and 11 rebounds against Bryant on November 12, 2012.<ref name="bio" /> On December 1, he injured his knee and missed the second half against [[Mississippi State name="my-story" /> He scored a season-high 33 points and was 7-of-14 from 3-point territory against [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]] on December 22.<ref name="bio" /> He led the [[Big East Conference]] in scoring with 18.3 points per game, becoming the fifth Friar all-time to lead the league in scoring.<ref name=bigeast>{{cite web|last=Bell|first=Ken|url=http://www.abc6.com/story/21568264/bryce-cotton-first-team-all-big-east-kadeem-batts-honorable-mention|title=Bryce Cotton First Team All-Big East, Kadeem Batts Honorable 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He subsequently earned first-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] honors.<ref name="bigeast" /> In total, Cotton averaged 19.7 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 37.8 minutes per game over 32 games.<ref name="stats" />

During the off-season, Cotton had surgery to repair his meniscus.<ref name="my-story" />

===Senior season===
To conclude the 2013–14 regular season, Cotton was the only player in the nation to average more than 40 minutes per game (40.1), having averaged 41.9 minutes in Big East competition.<ref name="nytimes2" /> His high minutes per game were as a result of Providence's six overtime games, four of which went to a second overtime. In those four double-overtime outings, Cotton played 200 minutes of a possible 200 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|last=Hamilton|first=Brian|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/one-and-one/2014/03/07/bryce-cotton-minutes-providence-friars-ncaa-tournament|title=Bryce Cotton not taking breathers in quest to get Providence back to NCAA tourney|work=SI.com|date=March 7, 2014|access-date=June 7, 2018}}</ref> His tireless play carried the Friars to their best season in a decade, as they headed into the Big East tournament with a 20–11 record.<ref name="nytimes2" /> After going 3–0 in the [[2014 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]], the Friars reached the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2004.<ref name="nytimes2" /> It marked Providence's first Big East tournament title since 1994, and Cotton was selected as the tournament MVP.<ref>{{cite web|last=O'Connell|first=Jim|url=http://www.abc6.com/story/24986916/bryce-cotton-leads-friars-to-the-big-east-tournament-championship|title=Bryce Cotton not taking breathers in quest to get Providence back to NCAA tourney|work=abc6.com|date=March 16, 2014|access-date=June 7, 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612140527/http://www.abc6.com/story/24986916/bryce-cotton-leads-friars-to-the-big-east-tournament-championship|archive-date=June 12, 2018}}</ref> In Providence's 79–77 loss to [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] in the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], Cotton scored a career-high 36 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400546909|title=Bryce Cotton lights up Tar Heels, fumbles away Friars' final shot|work=ESPN.com|date=March 21, 2014|access-date=June 7, 2018}}</ref>

In 35 games as a senior, Cotton averaged 21.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 5.9 assists and 1.0 steals per game.<ref name="stats" /> He led the Big East in assists and was second in scoring.<ref name="my-story" /> He subsequently earned first-team All-Big East honors for the second straight season,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigeast.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030914aaa.html|title=All-BIG EAST Men's Basketball Team Announced|work=BigEast.com|date=March 9, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140310130612/http://www.bigeast.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030914aaa.html|archive-date=March 10, 2014}}</ref> as well as being named to the AP Honorable Mention All-America Team. He finished his career ranked fourth all-time in scoring at Providence (1,975 points),<ref name=spurs-sign>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/140707_spurs_sign_bryce_cotton|title=Spurs Sign Rookie Bryce Cotton|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2014|access-date=July 7, 2014}}</ref> and became the fifth player from a major conference to average 20-plus points and five-or-more assists in a season since 2002.<ref name=jazz-sign>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-jack-cooley-and-bryce-cotton-10-day-contracts|title=Jazz Sign Jack Cooley and Bryce Cotton to 10-Day Contracts|work=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2015|access-date=February 24, 2015}}</ref>

Cotton graduated from Providence with a 3.1 [[Grading in education|GPA]] in [[sociology]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Hansen|first=Greg|url=https://tucson.com/former-badger-moore-lands-full-ride-at-nmsu/article_13b66c5f-6e7e-54d5-acbf-eea8429730e0.html|title=Former Badger Moore lands full ride at NMSU|work=tucson.com|date=August 17, 2014|access-date=December 2, 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===NBA, D-League, China, and Turkey (2014–2016)===
After going undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]], Cotton signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on July 7, 2014.<ref name="spurs-sign" /> He played in six [[2014 NBA Summer League|Summer League]] games and five preseason games for San Antonio, before being waived on October 23, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-waive-bryce-cotton-and-josh-davis|title=Spurs Waive Bryce Cotton and Josh Davis|work=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2014|access-date=October 23, 2014}}</ref> He subsequently joined San Antonio's [[NBA Development League]] affiliate team, the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/spurs_draft_results_2014_11_01.html|title=AUSTIN SPURS SELECT ERIK MURPHY IN THE FIRST ROUND OF THE 2014 NBA D-LEAGUE DRAFT|work=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141107155316/http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/spurs_draft_results_2014_11_01.html|archive-date=November 7, 2014}}</ref> He appeared in 34 games (all starts) for Austin in the [[2014–15 NBA Development League season|2014–15 season]], averaging 22.4 points (third in the D-League), 4.7 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.3 steals in 40.5 minutes (first in the D-League) per contest. He scored in double figures on 31 occasions and recorded 20-plus points in 20 games. He also registered 40-or-more points twice, including a season-high 43 points, eight rebounds, nine assists and two steals against the [[Reno Bighorns]] on February 19, 2015. He was named D-League Performer of the Week on February 23 after averaging 30.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 5.3 assists and 1.3 steals for the week.<ref name="jazz-sign" /> For the season, he was named to the Western Conference All-Star team for the [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|title=Thirteen NBA Veterans Headline Rosters for NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented by Kumho Tire|work=NBA.com|date=February 4, 2015|access-date=February 15, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150205023335/http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|archive-date=February 5, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> and earned [[All-NBA Development League Team|All-NBA D-League Second Team]] and NBA D-League All-Rookie First Team honors.<ref name=suns-sign>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-bryce-cotton|title=Suns Sign Bryce Cotton|work=NBA.com|date=November 25, 2015|access-date=November 25, 2015}}</ref>

On February 24, 2015, Cotton signed a 10-day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref name="jazz-sign" /> He made his NBA debut three days later, recording three points, two rebounds, one assist and one steal in just under seven minutes off the bench in a 104–82 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20150227/UTADEN/gameinfo.html|title=Favors has 21 points, 10 rebounds for Jazz|work=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2015|access-date=February 27, 2015}}</ref> He signed a second 10-day contract with the Jazz on March 6,<ref>{{cite ====2017–18 season: NBL MVP====
After attempting to re-enter the NBA via minicamps and the [[2017 NBA Summer League|Summer League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/bryce-cotton-joins-atlanta-hawks-summer-league/|title=Bryce Cotton joins Atlanta Hawks for Summer League|work=NBL.com.au|date=June 20, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170626222344/http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/bryce-cotton-joins-atlanta-hawks-summer-league/|archive-date=June 26, 2017}}</ref> Cotton made the decision to return to Perth, re-signing with the Wildcats for [[2017–18 NBL season]] on July 14, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wildcats.com.au/perth-wildcats/bryce-cotton-confirmed-return-perth/|title=BRYCE COTTON CONFIRMED TO RETURN TO PERTH|work=Wildcats.com.au|date=July 14, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170714072344/http://www.wildcats.com.au/perth-wildcats/bryce-cotton-confirmed-return-perth/|archive-date=July 14, 2017}}</ref> Cotton was considered a long-shot to re-join the Wildcats and reportedly turned down an offer from Spanish club [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Robinson|first=Chris|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/basketball/nbl-grand-final-mvp-bryce-cotton-in-line-for-shock-perth-wildcats-return-ng-b88536623z|title=NBL grand final MVP Bryce Cotton in line for shock Perth Wildcats return|work=[[The West Australian]]|date=July 13, 2017|access-date=July 14, 2017}}</ref>

In the Wildcats' season opener on October 7, Cotton scored a game-high 24 points in a 96–86 win over the [[Brisbane Bullets]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Davis|first=Greg|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/nbl-perth-wildcats-beat-brisbane-bullets-9686/news-story/54e910e96d62f6c3ce650cb496c7b86e|title=NBL: Perth Wildcats beat Brisbane Bullets 96-86|work=FoxSports.com.au|date=October 7, 2017|access-date=October 7, 2017}}</ref> On December 10, he scored a season-high 36 points in a 99–91 win over the [[Illawarra Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/38779-cotton-stars-to-continue-hawks-torture|title=Cotton stars to continue Hawks torture|work=NBL.com.au|date=December 10, 2017|access-date=December 10, 2017}}</ref> In the Wildcats' regular-season finale on February 18, Cotton scored a game-high 24 points with six 3-pointers and six assists in an 89–61 win over the [[Cairns Taipans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/40337-confidence-booster-for-cats-heading-to-finals|title=Confidence-booster for 'Cats Heading to Finals|work=NBL.com.au|date=February 18, 2018|access-date=February 18, 2018}}</ref> The Wildcats finished the regular season in third place with a 16–12 record, while Cotton finished as the NBL's leader in 3-pointers made with 84. The mark came from 187 attempts, giving him a 3-point shooting percentage of 44.9 – the best in the league for any player taking an average of at least one attempt per game. His 84 3-pointers was also third-most in Wildcats history for a regular season, behind [[Jermaine Beal]] (87, 2014) and [[James Harvey (basketball)|James Harvey]] (85, 2006). In July 2019, Cotton applied for an Australian Distinguished Talent visa, as [[Basketball Australia]] worked to secure his eligibility for the 2020 Olympics.<ref>{{cite web|last=O'Donoghue|first=Craig|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/perth-wildcats/fatherhood-and-citizenship-beckon-wildcats-star-bryce-cotton-ng-b881283584z|title=Fatherhood and citizenship beckon Wildcats star Bryce Cotton|work=[[The West Australian]]|date=August 7, 2019|access-date=August 7, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=O'Donoghue|first=Craig|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/perth-wildcats/perth-wildcats-star-bryce-cottons-citizenship-application-to-drag-out-beyond-nbl-deadline-for-roster-changes-c-9257089|title=Perth Wildcats star Bryce Cotton's citizenship application to drag out beyond NBL deadline for roster changes|work=[[The West Australian]]|date=December 23, 2022|access-date=January 27, 2023|quote=Cotton initially applied for a Distinguished Talent Visa in July 2019...}}</ref> At the time, Cotton believed that obtaining [[Australian permanent resident|permanent residency]] through the Distinguished Talent visa (DTV) would expedite the process for [[Australian citizenship]].<ref name=denied>{{cite web|last=O'Donoghue|first=Craig|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/basketball/perth-wildcats-star-bryce-cotton-denied-citizenship-after-government-says-he-was-in-australia-illegally--c-10228794|title=Perth Wildcats star Bryce Cotton denied citizenship after Government says he was in Australia illegally|work=[[The West Australian]]|date=April 3, 2023|access-date=April 3, 2023|url-access=subscription}}</ref> However, delays quickly arose due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
